Exploring patterns

For exploring, not confirming. This page screens 163 measures (74 main, the rest per topping) across every way of grouping people that the data allow, so some differences will look large by chance. Effect sizes are Cliff's δ (−1 to 1: how often a value from the group is higher than one from the comparison, minus how often it is lower; for yes/no measures, the difference in percentages). p comes from a Mann-Whitney test (by permutation for groups under 8), q is the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate within each grouping, and the intervals are bootstrap 95% intervals. Treat what stands out as a lead to test in a new sample or a preregistered analysis.

60 pizzas.

Leads for a larger study

The largest group differences in these data, one per measure. Each could become a hypothesis. The last two columns give how many people per group a two-group study needs for 80% power at α = .05 (two-sided), if the true δ is as large as seen here, and if it is half that size (effects found by screening many measures in a small sample are usually overestimated; plan with the second).
